name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,109

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
something assumed is implied rather than stated
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: A son takes on a naive outlook he did not have before.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is a lack of sophistication, an artless plainness of mind, which is one sense of the solution.

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled up, so the word beside it is rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, all four letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl is left bewildered by an unfamiliar dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a lively Latin American partner dance, so it is an example of the general word.

indicators.note: distressed suggests something knocked about and out of shape, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: every letter of these two words, apostrophe ignored, is the fodder

explanation.surface: A worried mother's warning sets off chaos in the household.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is literally a violent whirlpool and figuratively a state of confused, violent upheaval.

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word backing another sits beneath it, supporting it from below

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
to moderate pain is to ease it

explanation.surface: A moderate figure supports a Liberal's agreement, like a political deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like political support, but it only places the first word below the second in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A lease is a legal agreement letting property for a set period, a kind of written contract.

clue.text: Impose an upper limit on 50 per cent of cars parking

indicators.note: fifty per cent means half, so only the front half of the word is kept

blocks.note: the front two of its four letters
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A council wants to limit how many cars can park.
explanation.definitionFit: To cap spending or prices is to set a ceiling that the amount may not rise above.

indicators.note: engineered means constructed or contrived, so the letters are built into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, all seven letters

explanation.surface: A politician has plotted to betray his country.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the crime of betraying one's own country or sovereign, the gravest kind of disloyalty.

clue.text: Part of paper for those who’ve passed?

definitions.text: Part of paper for those who’ve passed?

blocks.clueFragment: Part of paper for those who’ve passed?
blocks.note: surface reading: a section of an exam paper meant for students who have passed
setter's reading: passed away, so the newspaper section reporting deaths

explanation.surface: Sounds like a portion of an exam reserved for successful candidates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed' suggests exams; here it is the euphemism for dying, and the paper is a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers print notices of recent deaths with short life stories in a dedicated section.

blocks.note: to ring is to sound a bell; a ring on the phone is also a bell
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An English beauty is given a ring, perhaps an engagement.
explanation.definitionFit: A belle is a beautiful woman, especially the most admired one at a gathering.

clue.text: Most liberal pals met after disturbance

indicators.note: after being disturbed, letters are thrown out of their original order

blocks.note: the fodder, all seven letters

explanation.surface: Friends met up after some trouble and were very generous.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal here means generous or plentiful, as in a liberal helping, so the most liberal is the most abundant.

clue.text: Waiter under sentence? His views are fickle

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a person rather than a noun

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word under another follows it in the grid

blocks.note: doing time is serving a prison sentence
a waiter serves at table

explanation.surface: A waiter sent to prison has opinions that change with the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A timeserver is someone who adapts their opinions to suit whoever holds power, an opportunist with no fixed principles.

clue.text: Sat inert, shocked about new brief

indicators.note: something shocked is jolted out of place, so these letters are rearranged
about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the next item

blocks.note: the fodder, all eight letters
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone sat motionless, stunned by some fresh news.
explanation.definitionFit: Transient means passing quickly or lasting only a short time, so it matches brief as an adjective.

blocks.note: to turn into something is to change
to table a proposal is to present it formally

explanation.surface: Swap a gift for a vinyl record player.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotating platter of a gramophone, and by extension the whole deck, plays vinyl records.

indicators.note: initially points at the start, so only the opening letter of each word is used

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: An outcome drove the two of us crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is the total got by adding, the outcome or result of a calculation.

clue.text: Provide part of meatloaf for dinner

indicators.note: part of means only a section of the following words is used

blocks.note: found running across the end of meatloaf, the whole of for, and the start of dinner

explanation.surface: Serve some meatloaf as the evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To afford can mean to supply or yield, as in trees affording shade, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Ostentatious display of food for supporter?

indicators.note: for here means intended for, placing the thing given beside its recipient

blocks.note: a fan supports a team or performer
fare is food and drink, as in simple fare

explanation.surface: A showy spread of snacks laid on for a sports fan.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: the answer is literally a supporter's food.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanfare is a flourish of trumpets and, by extension, a showy fuss or publicity.

blocks.note: first meaning: permits or concedes, a verb
second meaning: sums of money given, a plural noun

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words look like a sentence about permitting perks; they are two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb for conceding or permitting and the plural noun for awarded funding such as student bursaries.

clue.text: Writer referring to tiny amount charged

blocks.note: the writer of the clue refers to themselves as I
on can mean about or concerning, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: An author talks about a small fee they were billed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' suggests a bill; here it means electrically charged.
explanation.definitionFit: An ion is an atom or molecule carrying an electric charge, a minute particle.

clue.text: Go-between taking time for Marcus Aurelius?

definitions.note: a definition by example, flagged by the question mark

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the first word holds the next one inside it

blocks.note: a mediator goes between two parties in a dispute
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An intermediary takes his time over a Roman emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: Marcus Aurelius was the Roman emperor whose private reflections are known as the Meditations.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing the Meditations makes the philosopher-emperor an example of someone given to deep contemplation.

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the second

blocks.note: a door is an entrance
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A patron's name is carved over a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor gives money or goods to a cause, which is what a benefactor does.

clue.text: Less adventurous rogue back with me on board

indicators.note: back means the word for rogue is read in the opposite direction
on board means carried inside, so one item sits within the other

blocks.note: a rat is a scoundrel or rogue
taken as written

explanation.surface: A villain who has turned back, with me aboard, is less daring.
explanation.definitionFit: Tame describes something mild and unexciting, so the comparative means more timid or less bold.

blocks.note: to spar is to fight, as boxers do in practice
a tan is skin darkened by the sun

explanation.surface: A painful scrap made worse by burnt skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartan means austere and severe, after the famously frugal and disciplined people of ancient Sparta.

indicators.note: hiding means the word before it conceals the solution among its letters

blocks.note: sits in the second to fourth letters

explanation.surface: A stammer conceals a disapproving sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A tut is the clicking sound of the tongue made to express mild annoyance or reproach.

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of the following word is kept

blocks.note: to bomb a building is to destroy it
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: Wolf down the end of a sponge dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demolish' suggests eating greedily, matching the pudding; here it is destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombe is a dome-shaped frozen dessert, usually ice cream moulded in layers; pudding is the British word for dessert.

clue.text: Term shortened on approval twelve months in the past

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase defining a noun meaning past times

indicators.note: shortened means cut, so the word before it loses its final letter
in an across clue, one item on another comes straight after it

blocks.note: yes signals approval
taken as written before cutting
a year is twelve months

explanation.surface: A school term was cut short after approval a year ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesteryear is a literary word for past times or the recent past, as in the snows of yesteryear.
